symptom: 47 canonical_gf rows of multi-isotope species publish a log_gf that sits a CONSTANT offset above their own gf_linelist_vald sibling column, and that constant is log10 of a small integer equal to the number of stable isotopes: Nd II 38 rows at +0.8451 (x7.000), Sm II 4 rows at +0.8451 (x7.000), Eu II 5 rows at +0.3005 (x2.00), La II 1 row at +0.3010 (x2.00). RYA-1075 RE-DERIVED THE SET FROM THE SOURCE and found 54, not 47: the sibling-difference test RYA-1070 used misses rows with no VALD sibling (5 Nd II) and mis-measures the offset where the sibling itself differs (Ba II 4934, Cu I 5782). La II 5971 is NOT this defect - it is a duplicated row in the GES source, which also sums to +log10(2).
expected_behavior: The published log_gf of an HFS-collapsed line is log10 of the summed component gf of ONE isotope, i.e. the transition total, matching the primary laboratory value
actual_behavior: The published value is the transition total multiplied by the isotope count. 34 of the 47 are adjudicated directly by linemake: gf_linelist_vald reproduces linemake primary-lab declared totals (Lawler 2001 Eu II, Den Hartog 2003 Nd II, Lawler 2006 Sm II) to 0.0000-0.0006 dex while the published value is high by exactly log10(n_isotopes). 13 more carry the identical signature with no linemake counterpart to referee them
root_cause: IDENTIFIED (RYA-1075): pipeline/gf_resolver.cluster_physical_lines is isotope-blind - it groups on species + EP + wavelength gap, and two isotopes of one transition share the lower level and sit milli-Angstroms apart, so they land in ONE cluster. The GES v6 source is RYA-684 form (A): isotope-coded, each isotope carrying the FULL gf. Any consumer that then writes log10(sum 10**gf) over that cluster gets n_isotopes x the physical gf. Demonstrated end-to-end on Eu II 6645: 11 components, isotope 151 summing to +0.1199 and 153 to +0.1198, naive all-component sum +0.4208 == the published value exactly, gf-weighted centroid 6645.0905 == the published wavelength exactly. NOT RYA-684 - that is an ENGINE-side isotopfrac double-application with offset -log10(sum f_i^2); this is CONSUMER-side with offset log10(n). La II separates them: +0.0008 vs +0.3010.
detected_by: RYA-1070 linemake cross-reference, isotope_multiplier_scan (scripts/rya_linemake_xref.py)
affected_artifacts: data/audit/linemake_xref/isotope_multiplier_suspects.csv; data/audit/linemake_xref/provenance.json
science_impact: NO published value moves. The inflation was INERT: gf_resolver.apply_to_synth_array shifted each cluster by canon_total - cur_total and computed cur_total with the SAME isotope-blind sum, so both sides were equally inflated and the shift was 0.0000 - the delivered components passed through untouched. That is why RYA-684 correctly found the GES surface reached no live value. 🔴 CORRECTING THE TABLE ALONE WOULD HAVE MADE THE SHIFT -log10(n) AND SCALED EVERY COMPONENT DOWN BY n, turning a cancelling error into a live one; RYA-1075 therefore ships gf_resolver.physical_total in the same change. Measured after: the effective gf reaching Turbospectrum is bit-identical for all 5 Eu II rows, and A(Eu) (RYA-565: 0.702 HARPS / 0.603 IAG) is unchanged because that harness already synthesised on the per-isotope total.
notes_provenance: linemake 61af45bd8293c91059360cbb0cfa2d16d34fc21e; canonical_gf.csv sha256 3f87cfe8c64fa489771e8a5be52c046e414b847dd9eec559faf71cee3d66e8a4. NOT CORRECTED - RYA-161 validate-don't-tune. Three control rows (gf_098784, gf_098793, gf_120225) in the same species and the same source files published the VALD value instead and agree with linemake to 0.0000 dex | RYA-1075: 54 rows corrected to the per-isotope total (Nd II 43, Eu II 5, Sm II 4, Ba II 1, Cu I 1); 13 multi-isotope clusters REJECTED with reasons, incl. Li I 6707 (isotopes do not each carry the full gf - the positive control) and 4 rows already carrying the correct value. Guard installed as check_stewardship invariant 10, which re-detects from the SOURCE rather than pinning line_ids. Provenance sidecar: data/linelists/canonical_gf_isotope_corrections_rya1075.csv.

product_identity: pipeline/gf_resolver.apply_to_synth_array - effective gf delivered to Turbospectrum
symptom: Every multi-isotope cluster reached the engine with an effective gf EXACTLY log10(n_isotopes) TOO WEAK: Cu I -0.3010, Ba II -0.6990, Nd II/Sm II -0.8451. 12 clusters affected on main.
expected_behavior: apply_to_synth_array shifts a cluster so the gf the ENGINE ends up synthesising equals the canonical total for that line
actual_behavior: It normalised the isotope-BLIND cluster sum to canonical. Turbospectrum then applies isotopfrac per isotope and synthesises the PER-ISOTOPE total, which is log10(n) below the number that was normalised - so the effective gf came out log10(n) low. Measured main-vs-branch on all 67 multi-isotope clusters: 12 change, by exactly +log10(n); the other 55 change by <=7e-05.
